paper.title_en: Investigation of transfer coupling strength in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Hf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>178</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction
paper.abstract_en: Disentangling the effects of nucleon transfer via <math><mi>Q</mi></math> value and deformation on fusion has been a longstanding objective. To address this, a comparative analysis of the barrier distribution, which is an alternative probe to fusion, for the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Hf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>178</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Hf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>178</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> systems have been performed. The consistent alteration in deformation by choosing the same target <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Hf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>178</mn></mmultiscripts></math> mitigates its influence, thereby allowing for an explicit investigation of the effect of the <math><mi>Q</mi></math> value of nucleon transfer for these above systems. Consequently, the quasielastic scattering was measured for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Hf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>178</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> at backward angles. The extracted excitation function and barrier distribution were analyzed in light of coupled-channel calculations, which indicated a significant contribution from the one- and two-neutron transfer channels, alongside the rotational degrees of freedom in the highly deformed <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Hf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>178</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus. Furthermore, the coupling strength was extracted using the chi-square minimization method, yielding a value <math><mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.201</mn></mrow></math>. The extracted coupling strength of <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Hf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>178</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> system was compared with that of the two-neutron transfer in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Hf</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>178</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> system, which indicates that the coupling strength for nucleon transfer decreases with an increase in the <math><mi>Q</mi></math> value. This observed behavior might be due to the spectroscopic structures of the <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. The present study indicates that the spectroscopic properties play a significant role, along with <math><mi>Q</mi></math> values, in influencing the fusion reaction dynamics.
